Meningioma: The histopathological findings of uniform partly spindle-shaped tumor cells with oval nuclei and intranuclear clear inclusions, along with the presence of whorl formation and psammoma bodies, are suggestive of a meningioma. The weak expression of EMA, vimentin, and S-100 on immunohistochemistry also supports this diagnosis.
Solitary Fibrous Tumor: Although less likely, Solitary Fibrous Tumor could be considered due to the presence of uniform partly spindle-shaped tumor cells, but the specific features of whorl formation, psammoma bodies, and the immunohistochemical profile more strongly support Meningioma.
